about: Point-in-time operation-level diff between this repo's openapi.yaml and the contract the gateway publishes. It is a dated receipt, not a live view: regenerate with `node .github/scripts/published-drift.mjs openapi.yaml --out contract-drift.json`. The published-contract-drift workflow uploads a fresh copy on every scheduled run. The PUBLISHED half of this receipt ages on the gateway's schedule and only the scheduled drift job can refresh it; the REPO half is pinned by sources.repoOperationsDigest, which the freshness job checks offline on every run so this file cannot quietly disagree with the openapi.yaml sitting next to it.

allowlisted.justification: Same reasoning and same measurement date as DELETE /videos/{videoId}/chapters/{chapterId}: live-probed and confirmed answering, not ROUTE_NOT_MAPPED, but absent from the published /openapi.json document. A gap in the service's own spec generation. Lapses (and should be deleted) the moment the published document lists this operation.

Measured live 2026-09-06: this repo declares the operation (no x-schema-status: draft — marking it draft would be a FALSE claim) and the published /openapi.json document does not list it, but the live-behaviour probe tier confirms the gateway genuinely answers for it (not the ROUTE_NOT_MAPPED an absent route returns). The route is live; only the SERVICE's published spec generation has not yet registered it. This is the mirror image of the operations whose real repo descriptions the service overwrites — a gap in what the service publishes, not in what this repo declares. Lapses (and should be deleted) the moment the published document lists this operation.

The service's own generated 400 response for this operation is a single, coarser schema ($ref Error) with a shorter description; openapi.yaml documents a oneOf of the WAVE error envelope AND the RFC 8628 §3.5 device-flow error passthrough (authorization_pending / slow_down / expired_token / access_denied / invalid_grant) verbatim, which is the actual, more detailed behavior of this endpoint. This is the service's own OpenAPI reflection being less precise than this repo's hand-written documentation, not a real behavioral difference this repo needs to walk back. Keyed on the exact current published 400 description so a real future change to the service's generated shape still surfaces as drift rather than being silently re-exempted.

The gateway still serves the auto-generated skills-index open placeholder shape (not x-schema-status: draft — that means 'not observed live' here) for this operation (lowercase tag, no operationId, a summary that says 'draft — see api-spec for the full shape' and literally defers to this repo). openapi.yaml has since promoted this to a fully hand-documented /v1 operation (real params, description, Streams tag, operationId listStreams) ahead of the gateway shipping the matching handler. Exempt only while the published operation still has no operationId — the moment the gateway ships the real handler and starts publishing one, this predicate fails and the exemption lapses so the two shapes get compared for real.

Same shape and same reasoning as GET /streams: the published operation is still the auto-generated open placeholder shape (not x-schema-status: draft — that means 'not observed live' here) (no operationId), while openapi.yaml documents the real, hand-specified /v1 operation (operationId createStream) ahead of the gateway shipping it. Lapses the moment the published operation gains an operationId.

One of the 9 dead path families with no destination this PR deprecates in openapi.yaml (wave-gateway#1912, "8 advertised path families have no destination"): live-probed 2026-09-28, the gateway answers 404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND for this path on every method, so the operation is marked deprecated: true / x-status: unrouted here, its 402 (where declared) replaced with a documented 404, and its summary gets a (unrouted) suffix. The published /openapi.json document has not been regenerated to match yet (its own contract generation does not check for a destination either -- the same root cause #1912 fixes on the gateway side) and still shows this operation as though it were live. Keyed on the published side's deprecated field being absent, exactly as this repo declared it before this PR: the moment the service's own generation starts marking the operation deprecated too, this predicate fails and the two shapes get compared for real.

KEY COLLISION between two distinct operations that happen to share the literal path+method 'GET /usage' in their respective documents. openapi.yaml documents the real, tenant-scoped /v1 billing endpoint (tag Billing, operationId getUsage, usage:read scope) added independently of this exemption. The gateway ALSO serves a gateway-native, operator-only telemetry endpoint at the bare host root (tag internal, WAVE service bearer, no /v1 prefix) that this repo cannot document at this same key without overwriting the real customer endpoint's declaration — the two must live at the same path string in the published document because the operator route was never given a distinguishing per-operation servers override (unlike its siblings /leaderboard and /platform, which do carry one). This entry exempts ONLY the operator shape (matched by its 'internal' tag, which never appears on the real customer operation); it lapses the moment the published operation at this key stops being tagged internal, forcing a fresh look rather than silently re-exempting whatever answers here.

Keyed on the exact published summary so a real content change to this operation still surfaces as drift.

normalizationRules: strip op['x-version'] and op['x-deprecation-policy'], which the service assigns onto every operation
drop op['description'] on BOTH sides when the published value is the versioning boilerplate, and count the repo descriptions it destroyed
strip op.operationId only when it equals the service synthesis of (path, method) and this repo has none
strip responses 400/401/403/404/429 only when they deep-equal the injected error envelope and this repo lacks the code

drop responses 400/401/403/404/429 on BOTH sides when the published value deep-equals the injected error envelope but this repo declares a DIFFERENT response for that code — the service overwrote a real declaration, and count which codes it destroyed
unwrap the auto-wrapped 200 only when it deep-equals the wrapping of this repo's 200

strip a parameter's description/example on BOTH sides when every other field of that parameter (name, in, required, schema) is otherwise identical — the service publishes the contract faithfully and drops only prose
components.securitySchemes: NOT APPLICABLE — this comparator is operation-scoped and never reads components

root-level operations the service adds of its own accord are deliberately NOT normalized away: they surface as undocumented-live findings and must be allowlisted by path+method with a justification, so they stay visible
